enrichment.original_background: By a Final Decree dated 21 August 1996 entered in District Court Galle in Partition case No.2367/P Nimal, Sunil, Aruni and Kusum were allotted with 5/12th,5/12th, 1/12th and 1/12th shares respectively from and out of divided and defined lots 6 and 7 in Partition Plan No.185 dated 23rd June 1995 made by J.W. de Silva Licensed Surveyor By Deed of Transfer. No.346 dated 6th June 1998 attested by Ranjith Perera Notary Public Nimal purchased the 1/12th share of Aruni. Nimal was married to Nalini and had 3 children namely Amal, Bimal and Krishni. Nimal had a daughter named Achini by his first wife Malini, Nimal died intestate on 23rd April 2008. Within a year thereafter Nalini too died intestate. Nimal's son Bimal who was married to Amali died on 4th of March 2010 having met with an accident and issueless.

gold_answer_draft.issue: How did Nimal's half share of divided lots 6 and 7 devolve on his intestate death and on the successive intestate deaths of his widow Nalini and his son Bimal, so that a pedigree from Nimal to the present owners can be drawn?
gold_answer_draft.rule: Intestate succession to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance s.21(1), the lots being immovable property within s.3. The Ordinance applies here because none of the exclusions in s.2 (Kandyan, Muslim, Thesawalamai) is disclosed, and the s.20 condition is met since every death and marriage in question post-dates the 1876 proclamation. On each intestacy the surviving spouse first takes one-half of the estate (s.22). Subject to that half, the right of inheritance runs in the order descendants, ascendants, collaterals (s.23). Children take equally per capita and the issue of a deceased child take per stirpes (s.24), and heirs equally near in degree take per capita (s.30). Where descendants fail, the estate goes to the parents (s.25); where both parents have also failed, it goes to the brothers and sisters, whether of the whole or half blood (s.26). Where the half-siblings are on one side only, s.27 directs that the full siblings take one half of that portion first and divide the other half with the half-siblings.
gold_answer_draft.application: Step 1 - Nimal's holding. Under the Final Decree of 21 August 1996 Nimal was allotted 5/12 of lots 6 and 7, and by Deed of Transfer No. 346 of 6 June 1998 he bought Aruni's 1/12. At his death he therefore held 5/12 + 1/12 = 6/12, that is a half share of the land. Sunil's 5/12 and Kusum's 1/12 are untouched by the deaths and remain with them. Step 2 - Nimal's intestacy, 23 April 2008. He left his widow Nalini and four children: Achini (by his first wife Malini), Amal, Bimal and Krishni. Nalini takes one-half of his estate under s.22, which is 1/4 of the land. Under ss.23, 24 and 30 the other half, also 1/4 of the land, is shared equally per capita among the four children, giving each child 1/16 of the land. Step 3 - Nalini's intestacy, within a year of April 2008. Her estate is the 1/4 she took from Nimal. Nimal had predeceased her, so there is no surviving spouse to take under s.22, and the whole estate passes to her descendants under ss.23, 24 and 30. Her children are Amal, Bimal and Krishni only; Achini is Nimal's daughter by Malini and is not a descendant of Nalini, so she takes nothing from this estate. Each of the three takes 1/4 divided by 3, that is 1/12 of the land. Immediately after this Amal, Bimal and Krishni each hold 1/16 + 1/12 = 7/48 of the land and Achini holds 1/16. Step 4 - Bimal's death, 4 March 2010, married to Amali and issueless. On the footing that he too died intestate, his estate of 7/48 devolves as follows. Amali takes one-half under s.22, that is 7/96 of the land. The remaining 7/96 must pass down the s.23 order: Bimal left no descendants, and under s.25 it would go to his parents, but both Nimal and Nalini were already dead, so under s.26 it goes to his brothers and sisters of the whole and half blood. Amal and Krishni are of the full blood; Achini is a half-sister on the father's side and there is no half-sibling on the mother's side. Section 27 therefore applies in its final limb: Amal and Krishni first take one half of the 7/96, that is 7/192, in equal shares of 7/384 each, and the other 7/192 is divided per capita among Amal, Krishni and Achini under ss.27 and 30, giving each of them 7/576. So from Bimal's estate Amal takes 7/384 + 7/576 = 35/1152, Krishni takes the same 35/1152, Achini takes 7/576 = 14/1152 and Amali takes 7/96 = 84/1152.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The pedigree runs: Nimal (holder of 6/12 of lots 6 and 7, being 5/12 under the Final Decree of 1996 plus 1/12 bought from Aruni by Deed No. 346 of 1998) died intestate on 23 April 2008 leaving his widow Nalini and four children, Achini (by his first wife Malini), Amal, Bimal and Krishni; Nalini took one-half of his estate and the four children the other half in equal shares. Nalini then died intestate within a year, and her share passed in equal shares to her own three children Amal, Bimal and Krishni, Achini being excluded as not her descendant. Bimal, married to Amali, then died on 4 March 2010 issueless and, on the footing that he died intestate, his share passed one-half to Amali as surviving spouse and the other half to his siblings, both parents having predeceased him: his full siblings Amal and Krishni taking one half of that portion between them and sharing the remaining half with his paternal half-sister Achini. The present owners of Nimal's half share are therefore Amal, Krishni, Achini and Amali, alongside the original co-owners Sunil and Kusum who are unaffected.

answer_claims.claim_text: Intestate inheritance to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance s.21(1), whatever the deceased's domicile, and the divided lots are immovable property within s.3.

The Ordinance's inheritance sections do not apply to Kandyans, Muslims or Tamils of the Northern Province subject to the Thesawalamai, and apply only to estates of persons dying after the 1876 proclamation who were then unmarried or married after it.
A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the property of a person who dies intestate.
Subject to the surviving spouse's half, the right of inheritance runs in the order descendants, then ascendants, then collaterals.
Children are preferent to all others in a parent's estate and take equally per capita, and heirs equally near in degree take per capita and not per stirpes.
Where an intestate leaves no descendants the estate goes to the parents, and where both parents have also failed it goes to the brothers and sisters, whether of the whole or half blood.
Where there are half-siblings on one side only, the full brothers and sisters take one half of the sibling portion in the first place and divide the other half with the half-siblings.
Nimal held 6/12 (a half share) of lots 6 and 7 at his death: 5/12 under the Final Decree of 21 August 1996 plus the 1/12 bought from Aruni by Deed of Transfer No. 346 of 6 June 1998.
On Nimal's intestate death on 23 April 2008 his widow Nalini took one-half of his estate and his four children Achini, Amal, Bimal and Krishni took the other half in equal shares.

On Nalini's intestate death within a year her share passed wholly to her descendants, namely her three children Amal, Bimal and Krishni in equal shares; Achini, being Nimal's daughter by Malini and not a descendant of Nalini, took nothing from Nalini's estate.

Bimal died on 4 March 2010 married to Amali and issueless, so his descendants failed; both his parents had already died, so no ascendant survived and his estate passed to his collaterals after his widow's half.

Bimal's siblings were his full brother Amal and full sister Krishni and his paternal half-sister Achini, with no half-sibling on the mother's side, so the full siblings took one half of the sibling portion first and shared the other half with Achini.

The pedigree of Nimal's half share is: Nimal, died intestate 23 April 2008, leaving widow Nalini (one-half) and children Achini, Amal, Bimal and Krishni (one-half between them); Nalini, died intestate within a year, leaving her share to Amal, Bimal and Krishni; Bimal, died 4 March 2010 issueless, leaving his share one-half to his widow Amali and one-half to his siblings Amal, Krishni and Achini in the proportions fixed by section 27.
The present owners of the land are Sunil and Kusum, whose original shares are unaffected, together with Amal, Krishni, Achini and Amali as the heirs in Nimal's line.
The final step of the pedigree assumes that Bimal died intestate, which the scenario does not state expressly, and that Achini was born of a lawful marriage between Nimal and Malini.

The remaining 7/96 must pass down the s.23 order: Bimal left no descendants, and under s.25 it would go to his parents, but both Nimal and Nalini were already dead, so under s.26 it goes to his brothers and sisters of the whole and half blood. Amal and Krishni are of the full blood; Achini is a half-sister on the father's side and there is no half-sibling on the mother's side. Section 27 therefore applies in its final limb: Amal and Krishni first take one half of the 7/96, that is 7/192, in equal shares of 7/384 each, and the other 7/192 is divided per capita among Amal, Krishni and Achini under ss.27 and 30, giving each of them 7/576. So from Bimal's estate Amal takes 7/384 + 7/576 = 35/1152, Krishni takes the same 35/1152, Achini takes 7/576 = 14/1152 and Amali takes 7/96 = 84/1152.

These six shares add up to 1152/1152, the whole of the land. Expressed as shares of Nimal's estate alone, Amal and Krishni take 203/576 each, Achini 86/576 and Amali 84/576. answer_claims.claim_text: Intestate inheritance to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance s.21(1), whatever the deceased's domicile, and the divided lots are immovable property within s.3.

The Ordinance's inheritance sections do not apply to Kandyans, Muslims or Tamils of the Northern Province subject to the Thesawalamai, and apply only to estates of persons dying after the 1876 proclamation who were then unmarried or married after it.
A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the property of a person who dies intestate.
Subject to the surviving spouse's half, the right of inheritance runs in the order descendants, then ascendants, then collaterals.
Children are preferent to all others in a parent's estate and take equally per capita, and heirs equally near in degree take per capita and not per stirpes.
Where an intestate leaves no descendants the estate goes to the parents, and where both parents have also failed it goes to the brothers and sisters, whether of the whole or half blood.
Where there are half-siblings on one side only, the full brothers and sisters take one half of the sibling portion in the first place and divide the other half with the half-siblings.
Nimal held 6/12 (a half share) of lots 6 and 7 at his death: 5/12 under the Final Decree of 21 August 1996 plus the 1/12 bought from Aruni by Deed of Transfer No. 346 of 6 June 1998.
On Nimal's intestate death on 23 April 2008 his widow Nalini took one-half of his estate and his four children Achini, Amal, Bimal and Krishni took the other half in equal shares.

On Nalini's intestate death within a year her share passed wholly to her descendants, namely her three children Amal, Bimal and Krishni in equal shares; Achini, being Nimal's daughter by Malini and not a descendant of Nalini, took nothing from Nalini's estate.

Bimal died on 4 March 2010 married to Amali and issueless, so his descendants failed; both his parents had already died, so no ascendant survived and his estate passed to his collaterals after his widow's half.

Bimal's siblings were his full brother Amal and full sister Krishni and his paternal half-sister Achini, with no half-sibling on the mother's side, so the full siblings took one half of the sibling portion first and shared the other half with Achini.
Each of Nimal's four children took 1/16 of the land from his estate and Nalini took 1/4 of the land.
Nalini's 1/4 divided equally among Amal, Bimal and Krishni gave each of them a further 1/12, so that each held 7/48 of the land while Achini held 1/16.

Of Bimal's 7/48, Amali took 7/96 as surviving spouse and the remaining 7/96 went to the siblings, of which Amal and Krishni took 7/192 between them in equal shares of 7/384 each, and Amal, Krishni and Achini shared the other 7/192 equally at 7/576 each.
The shares presently owned in lots 6 and 7 are Sunil 5/12, Kusum 1/12, Amal 203/1152, Krishni 203/1152, Achini 86/1152 (43/576) and Amali 84/1152 (7/96), which together make up the whole land.
Expressed as fractions of Nimal's former half share alone, Amal and Krishni take 203/576 each, Achini 86/576 and Amali 84/576.
The arithmetic assumes that Bimal died intestate, which the scenario does not state expressly, and that Achini was born of a lawful marriage between Nimal and Malini.
